comment:
Been looking to try different sandwiches places, and Babas deli has been on the list for a while. Coming from the west we’ve tried heaps of places, but we’d say this tops the list!

Pastrami - The most balanced pastrami sandwich i’ve had yet. It was the perfect ratio of pastrami, rocket, grilled peppers and mustard on the softest focaccia, and wasn’t too salty at all.

Vodka pizza schnitzel fold - Generous on the vodka sauce and cheese and it worked together perfectly. The pizza base, like the focaccia was light and airy and was the favourite order out of what we tried.

Cheese pizza slice - So simple but with the vodka sauce and heaping of cheese on top was so good!

Would recommend this place to anyone, prices are reasonable, with generous serving sizes and really friendly service.

The must get is defs the Mama's Vodka ($21) - Crumbed chicken, vodka sauce, parmesan lemon rocket & stracciatella cheese. It has a fatttt piece of chicken and pairs so well with the vodka chicken. We did try the special where it was in the fried pizza dough but prefer the focaccia, since the bread is so nice and fluffy.

The Pastrami ($23) was delicious as well and my friend loved her Spicy Tuna Melt. The Salami ($19) with spicy romesco sauce, herbed garlic mayo, pickled sumac onions & lemon parmesan rocket was nice and fresh but wasn't as wow factor as the chicken.

Service was lively and friendly and they really try to have a chat with all the patrons so it is a very inviting vibe.

comment:
Really disappointing first experience here. I’ve always enjoyed Hectors, so I was keen to give this place a shot, but unfortunately it completely missed the mark.

The sandwiches and toasties were mid (not the best but judging the standards in melbourne, this place is below average), but the venue itself felt extremely understaffed and poorly managed. There was no menu displayed on the wall and barely any printed menus available either. When we asked staff for a menu, they seemed unsure what to do because there genuinely wasn’t one in sight.

The space was also quite messy. Tables were left covered in rubbish like sandwich wrappers and empty drink cups, and there wasn’t even a bin available for customers to clear their own trash. It just made the whole experience feel chaotic and unorganised.

Such a shame. Overall it was a pretty terrible first impression.

comment:
I’m a little picky when it comes to sandwiches and very easily disappointed but I was rather impressed with Nico’s!

I’ve had many roasted vegetarian sandwiches and they’ve been quite bland with not much depth in the flavour. What really shown through was the sweet pickled eggplant, pickled onions and salsa to give it that sweet element. The cheese was neutral but balanced, and I loved the roasted peppers and rocket for that freshness. I tried 2 dishes, AUD 27 in total.
- Pastrami (AUD 18): the pastrami was soft, almost like uncrisped bacon, and didn’t really have that smoky flavour you’d expect. The toast was on the dry side, and the sauce wasn’t memorable. For a signature item, it didn’t leave much of an impression, except that it was quite salty with the extra seasoning on top.
- Popcorn Chicken (AUD 9) + Truffle Mayo (AUD 2): thin coating, not very crispy, but the chicken inside was juicy. This one works better with dipping sauce. If you like your chicken well-coated in sauce, you’ll probably need more than one.

Overall, not a bad experience, but not memorable enough for me to come back.

name: Sloppy Joe's
address: Shop 2/190 Queen St, Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia
comment:
Sloppy Joe’s by day, Floppy Joe’s by night — and honestly, both sides deliver.

We came in as a group of 7 (including 4 kids), and it handled us effortlessly. The all-you-can-eat fried chicken for $30 is an absolute steal, and the food itself, Next level. The chicken was incredible, especially the hot honey — that perfect mix of sweet heat that keeps you going back for more. Dangerous in the best way.

The sides were just as impressive and came out faster than you can say “thank you.” No waiting around, no chasing staff — just smooth, efficient service all night.

Speaking of service, it was spot on. Polite, friendly, and genuinely accommodating, especially with a bigger group and kids. You can tell they actually care about the experience, not just turning tables.

The place itself was clean, well-kept, and had a great energy to it. The vibe is relaxed and laid-back, but still lively enough to feel like you’re out somewhere worth being. Easy, comfortable, no pressure — just good food, good company, and a space that lets you enjoy both.

Highly recommend this spot — whether you’re going for a casual feed, bringing the family, or lining your stomach properly. We’ll definitely be back.

comment:
Stopped by Warkop Sandwich Bar and tried the Beef Brisket & Pickle with rendang sauce, American cheese, and light rye.

The sandwich was delicious, packed with flavour, and the rendang sauce really made it stand out. It was also the perfect size to share, making it a great option if you’re stopping in with someone else.

Unfortunately, they had sold out of the fried chicken sandwich, which was actually one of the main reasons for visiting. That said, if the brisket sandwich is anything to go by, I’ll definitely be back to give it a try.

The only downside is the location if you’re planning to dine in. The seating area overlooks a multi-level car park and the surrounding area isn’t particularly inviting.

For me, this is definitely a takeaway destination rather than a sit-down experience. Great food, plenty of flavour, and worth the visit for the sandwiches alone

name: Warkop Richmond
address: 12 Risley St, Richmond VIC 3121, Australia
comment:
My experience at Warkop was very average.
I tried the beef brisket and filet-o-fish sandwiches. The brisket, which I expected to channel rich, aromatic rendang flavours, was so salty to the point where it became overpowering. It left me more thirsty than satisfied, and unfortunately lacked the depth and complexity of rendang.
The filet-o-fish felt almost too familiar. It closely mirrors the maccas version, which isn’t inherently a bad thing, but there wasn’t enough of a twist or elevation to justify choosing it over its fast food counterpart.
Portion-wise, both sandwiches were smaller than expected. As someone who doesn’t usually finish a full sandwich in one sitting, I was surprised to polish these off without much effort.
Overall, it was an ok meal. Nothing off-putting, but nothing that stood out either. Warkop didn’t quite hit the mark in terms of flavour or value for me.
